title: Harness policy
description: The shape of .harness/policy.json. Fields group into four jobs — scope, command constraints, execution constraints and enforcement — which is a documentation outline rather than structure: the document stays flat so no field name depends on its group. Unknown keys are tolerated on purpose, because the runtime validator is permissive about fields it does not know and a schema that disagreed with it would be a second, silent definition. `rules` and `severityActions` may only tighten a rule's declared severity and action; the no-loosening rule is enforced by validatePolicy, since JSON Schema cannot compare them. See docs/decisions/ADR-004-policy-severity-rules.md and docs/decisions/ADR-008-policy-scope-and-deferred-rule-disposition.md.

allowedProductPaths.description: Scope. The only paths a coder may change. Prefix matching, so 'src/' means 'inside src/'.

protectedPaths.description: Scope. Paths that may never change, even when they are inside allowedProductPaths.

forbiddenCommands.description: Command constraints. Command patterns refused before execution, matched as contiguous token sequences.

allowedAgentCommands.description: Command constraints. Executable names a provider may use. Empty or absent means no restriction.

requiredChecks.description: Execution constraints. Package scripts that must exist and must pass as verification gates.

maxIterations.description: Execution constraints. The upper bound on coder retries.

agentTimeoutMs.description: Execution constraints. The bound on one provider invocation. Verification gates keep their own timeout.

maxChangedFiles.description: Execution constraints. The most files one coder iteration may change.

onViolation.description: Enforcement. Whether a violation fails the run or is only recorded. Never weakens side-effect control.

rules.description: Enforcement. Per-rule severity and action overrides, keyed by a rule id an implementation declares. A project may only tighten what the rule declared.

severityActions.description: Enforcement. Overrides the default severity-to-action mapping (error→reject, warning→review, info→report), tightening only.

maxSemanticCalls.description: Execution constraints. The most semantic review calls this run may make; absent means no budget. Running out skips warnings and fails closed on errors.
